items.title: Starting date shown
items.requirement: The programme shows the starting date.
items.finding: Programme start 2024-01-02.

items.title: Access dates shown
items.requirement: The programme shows the access dates for each part of the Site.
items.finding: No activity names reference access or possession.
items.recommendation: Access dates must appear as identifiable activities or milestones. If access is modelled under different wording, confirm it manually.

items.title: Key Dates shown
items.requirement: The programme shows the Key Dates stated in the Contract Data.
items.finding: 2 milestones in the programme; 0 named as a Key Date or sectional completion. No Key Dates were supplied to check against.
items.recommendation: Enter the Key Dates from Contract Data part 1 above, and make sure each has a corresponding milestone whose condition is met by the preceding work.

items.title: Completion Date and planned Completion
items.requirement: The programme shows the Completion Date and planned Completion, the difference between them being terminal float.
items.finding: Planned Completion is 2025-06-26. No Completion Date has been entered, so terminal float cannot be assessed.
items.recommendation: Enter the Completion Date from Contract Data part 1 above. NEC expects planned Completion to sit on or before it, and the gap to be shown as terminal float owned by the Contractor.

items.title: Order and timing of operations
items.requirement: The programme shows the order and timing of the operations which the Contractor plans to do in order to Provide the Works.
items.finding: 0 of 60 activities (0.0%) have a missing predecessor or successor, so their timing is not driven by the programme logic.

items.title: Order and timing of the work of the Client and Others
items.requirement: The programme shows the order and timing of the work of the Client and Others as last agreed, or as stated in the Scope.
items.finding: No activities appear to represent work by the Client or Others.
items.recommendation: NEC requires the Client's and Others' work to be shown. Without it the programme cannot demonstrate what the Contractor is waiting on, and cannot support a compensation event for late access or information.

items.title: Provisions for float
items.requirement: The programme shows provisions for float.
items.finding: 27 incomplete activities carry float; 5 of them are negative.
items.recommendation: Negative float means the programme does not show a workable path to Completion. Under NEC total float belongs to the project and is available to absorb compensation events — it cannot be negative before any have been assessed.

items.title: Provisions for time risk allowances
items.requirement: The programme shows provisions for time risk allowances.
items.finding: No activities are identifiable as time risk allowances.
items.recommendation: NEC expects time risk allowances to be visible as distinct items, not buried inside activity durations. Allowances hidden in durations cannot be demonstrated to the Project Manager and are hard to defend when a compensation event is assessed.

items.title: Dates needed — access to a part of the Site
items.requirement: The programme shows the dates when, in order to Provide the Works in accordance with the programme, the Contractor will need access to a part of the Site.
items.finding: No activities clearly reference access to a part of the Site.
items.recommendation: If access to a part of the Site is required, show it on the programme with the date needed, so late access can be identified against a stated need date. If genuinely not required, no action.

items.title: Dates needed — acceptances
items.requirement: The programme shows the dates when, in order to Provide the Works in accordance with the programme, the Contractor will need acceptances.
items.finding: No activities clearly reference acceptances.
items.recommendation: If acceptances is required, show it on the programme with the date needed, so late acceptance is measurable against the programme. If genuinely not required, no action.

items.title: Dates needed — Plant and Materials provided by the Client
items.requirement: The programme shows the dates when, in order to Provide the Works in accordance with the programme, the Contractor will need Plant and Materials provided by the Client.
items.finding: No activities clearly reference Plant and Materials provided by the Client.
items.recommendation: If Plant and Materials provided by the Client is required, show it on the programme with the date needed, so late free-issue supply can be evidenced. If genuinely not required, no action.

items.title: Dates needed — information from Others
items.requirement: The programme shows the dates when, in order to Provide the Works in accordance with the programme, the Contractor will need information from Others.
items.finding: 20 activities reference information from Others.
items.recommendation: Confirm each carries the date it is needed by, so late information can be evidenced.

items.title: Statement of how the work is done — resources
items.requirement: For each operation, a statement of how the Contractor plans to do the work identifying the principal Equipment and other resources which will be used.
items.finding: 3 of 26 remaining operations (11.5%) carry no resources or cost.
items.recommendation: Resource-load the remaining operations. Without resources the programme cannot evidence how the work will be done, which is an express requirement and a common ground for non-acceptance.

items.title: Health and safety requirements, and contract procedures
items.requirement: The programme shows provisions for health and safety requirements and the procedures set out in the contract.
items.finding: Cannot be determined from a programme file.
items.recommendation: Check by eye that the programme includes the health and safety provisions and contractual procedures — inspections, tests, submissions, Supervisor activities — required by the Scope.

items.title: Other information required by the Scope
items.requirement: The programme shows other information which the Scope requires.
items.finding: Cannot be determined from a programme file.
items.recommendation: Read the Scope's programme clause and confirm each additional requirement is present. This is the most commonly missed item.

items.title: Plans shown are practicable
items.requirement: A reason for not accepting: the Contractor's plans which it shows are not practicable.
items.finding: 2 hard constraints override the logic; 29 finish-to-start links were violated in execution.
items.recommendation: Hard constraints and out-of-sequence working suggest the programme does not describe how the work can actually be built. Remove the constraints and re-sequence to match how the work is really done.

items.title: Shows the information the contract requires
items.requirement: A reason for not accepting: it does not show the information which the contract requires.
items.finding: Assessed by the clause 31.2 items above, plus anything additional the Scope demands.
items.recommendation: Work through the 31.2 items above; every failure there is a defensible reason for the Project Manager not to accept.

items.title: Represents the Contractor's plans realistically
items.requirement: A reason for not accepting: it does not represent the Contractor's plans realistically.
items.finding: No evidence the programme contradicts its own data date.

items.title: Complies with the Scope
items.requirement: A reason for not accepting: it does not comply with the Scope.
items.finding: Cannot be determined from a programme file.
items.recommendation: Check sequencing constraints, sectional completion and method requirements in the Scope against the programme.

items.title: Actual progress achieved on each operation
items.requirement: The Contractor shows on each revised programme the actual progress achieved on each operation.
items.finding: 39 operations are started or complete; 0 of them have no actual start recorded.

items.title: Effect of progress on the timing of remaining work
items.requirement: The Contractor shows the effect of actual progress upon the timing of the remaining work.
items.finding: 0 activities carry actual dates after the data date; 3 incomplete activities are still forecast to finish before it.
items.recommendation: Remaining work must be forecast forward of the data date. Reschedule so incomplete operations sit in the future and no actual date is later than the data date.

items.title: Effects of compensation events
items.requirement: NEC4 dropped NEC3's express reference to implemented compensation events, but a revised programme must still show the effect of a compensation event that is already affecting the remaining work.
items.finding: No activities are identifiable as compensation events.
items.recommendation: If compensation events have been implemented, show their effect on the programme. Note that an un-implemented event affecting remaining work should move planned Completion, not the Completion Date.

items.title: How delays and notified Defects will be dealt with
items.requirement: The Contractor shows how it plans to deal with any delays and to correct notified Defects.
items.finding: No activities are identifiable as defect correction.
items.recommendation: Show defect correction and the plan for recovering any delay. A revised programme that shows slippage without a recovery plan invites rejection.

items.title: Other changes proposed to the Accepted Programme
items.requirement: The Contractor shows any other changes which it proposes to make to the Accepted Programme.
items.finding: Only one programme is loaded, so changes cannot be identified.
items.recommendation: Load the previous Accepted Programme in Trend or Baseline & Delay, and this will list what has changed.

items.title: Revised programmes submitted at the stated interval
items.requirement: The Contractor submits a revised programme at no longer interval than that stated in the Contract Data, from the starting date until Completion.
items.finding: No revision interval has been entered.
items.recommendation: Enter the interval from Contract Data part 1 above (commonly 4 weeks) and load your successive programmes to check compliance.
